chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who caught game while he was in ihram: may one who is not in ihram eat from it? He said: There is no problem; the expiation is only upon the muhrim.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand them to mean that when the muhrim catches the game while it is still alive, it is permissible for the non-muhrim to slaughter it and eat it; rather, what is forbidden to him is what the muhrim himself slaughters.

It is also possible that what is meant by them is that he kills the game by shooting it, and it is only forbidden when he takes it while it is alive and then slaughters it. On this interpretation, there is no contradiction between the reports, and that which confirms the earlier reports...

key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: game animal hunted in the sacred state
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted hadith reports under discussion
key_terms.الْحَلَالُ: one who is not in ihram, for whom ordinary lawful acts remain permitted
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: the expiatory compensation due for violating a restriction of ihram
key_terms.الْمُحِلِّ: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.يَذْبَحَهُ: slaughters it according to the relevant legal act

ai.seo_question: Can a non-muhrim eat game that was caught by a muhrim during ihram?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling concerning game caught by a muhrim during ihram. It indicates that the liability of expiation falls upon the muhrim, and it presents a reconciliation of reports by distinguishing between game slaughtered by the muhrim and game taken alive then slaughtered by a non-muhrim.
